question: Which CAPEC patterns map to ATT&CK technique T1021 (Remote Services), and what is that technique?

answer.headline: Gathered 2 record(s) from 2 source(s); 1 cross-source correlation(s) on shared identifiers.
answer.narrative: The CAPEC pattern Remote Services with Stolen Credentials (CAPEC-555) maps to the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1021. T1021, titled Remote Services, involves adversaries using valid accounts to log into services that accept remote connections, such as telnet, SSH, and VNC, to perform actions as the logged-on user.

results.query: MATCH (n:Technique) WHERE n.attack_id IN $ids OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r]-(m) WITH n, CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE type(r) END AS rel, CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE startNode(r) = n END AS outgoing, CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE head(labels(m)) END AS neighbour_label, count(m) AS cnt WITH n, collect(CASE WHEN rel IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE {rel: rel, outgoing: outgoing, label: neighbour_label, count: cnt} END) AS raw WITH n, [f IN raw WHERE f IS NOT NULL] AS facets RETURN n.attack_id AS id, n.name AS name, n.properties_json AS properties_json, facets AS facets LIMIT 300

records.name: Remote Services
records.label: Technique
records.description:
Adversaries may use [Valid Accounts](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078) to log into a service that accepts remote connections, such as telnet, SSH, and VNC. The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

In an enterprise environment, servers and workstations can be organized into domains. Domains provide centralized identity management, allowing users to login using one set of credentials across the entire network.
